title: Module 1 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

items.q: A researcher measures anxiety in 120 students at one university to learn about all college students. The 120 students are the
items.why: The sample is the group actually measured. The population is the larger group the researcher wants to describe.

items.q: A value that describes a sample, such as the mean anxiety of the 120 students, is called a
items.why: Statistics describe samples. Parameters describe populations.

items.q: A value that describes an entire population is called a
items.why: A parameter is a population value. It is usually unknown, which is why we estimate it from a sample statistic.

items.q: The difference between a sample statistic and the population parameter it estimates is
items.why: Sampling error is the natural discrepancy that arises because a sample is only part of the population.

items.q: Eye color recorded as brown, blue, green, or hazel is measured on which scale?
items.why: Categories with no order or numeric meaning are nominal.

items.q: Finishing positions in a race (1st, 2nd, 3rd) are measured on which scale?
items.why: Rank order is meaningful but the gaps between ranks are not necessarily equal, so the scale is ordinal.

items.q: Temperature in degrees Fahrenheit is measured on which scale?
items.why: Equal intervals but no true zero. Zero degrees Fahrenheit does not mean no temperature, so 80 is not twice as hot as 40.

items.q: Reaction time in milliseconds is measured on which scale?
items.why: Zero means no time, and ratios make sense. 600 ms is twice as long as 300 ms.

items.q: Which design includes random assignment of participants to conditions?
items.why: Random assignment is what defines a true experiment and is what supports cause and effect claims.

items.q: A variable that can take any value along a continuum, such as time or weight, is
items.why: Continuous variables can be divided into finer and finer units. Discrete variables take separate, countable values.
